$description: AUTHORED — frame patches: stackable PARTIAL egui::Frame values, resolved per-axis against a runtime Tone. Generated to frame_patches_gen.rs; hue/step refs are cross-validated at build (unknown → build fails). Composition (docs/design/doctrine.md): additive axes (shadows, back_glow, tints, anim) concatenate across the stack; override axes (fill, stroke, corner_radius, override_text_color, override_font_id) last-wins. A hovered/active/open block overlays that patch's axes for the state. Color refs: {tone:STEP} = the surface Tone's ladder at STEP; {hue:ID,step:STEP} = a fixed pool hue; {surface:SLOT} / {ink:SLOT} = a named slot; {black:true}; optional alpha (0-255, default 255). role: base = neubrutalist/claymorphic (one per surface); overlay = cyber/retro (ride on top). NOTE: cyber/retro animation (hue-drift/crt-flicker) is deferred until motion.json carries the effects + a cheap painter — anim is empty for now.
$naming: egui 0.35 has NO concept of a stackable partial look, so there is no egui term to adopt for one — inventing a word here is exactly what produced 'trait', a Rust KEYWORD that means something else entirely. The rule instead: name every axis for the egui field it lands on. The destination is egui::Frame (see paint_treated in src/lib.rs — .fill / .stroke / .corner_radius), never style::WidgetVisuals. Law: docs/plans/coldlight-naming-and-the-pattern-library.md.

$axes.shadows: epaint::Shadow — egui::Frame::shadow is SINGULAR, so stacking is a ColdLight extension of it

$states: egui::style::Widgets slot names, exactly: the patch itself is the INACTIVE state; hovered · active · open overlay it. `open` is admitted by the schema and authored by nothing yet — egui has it, so the axis exists rather than being discovered missing later.
$lineages: The five seed ancestrals — bauhaus · art-deco · swiss · aero · brutalist. PROVENANCE, never composable entries: a lineage records what a patch descends from, so a new patch is derived from ancestry instead of invented. Cross-validated at build against this list.

patches.label: Neubrutalist
patches.blurb: Flat saturated surface, crisp hard edge, hard offset shadow, lit-from-behind glow. Loud, honest, tappable — and cheap.

patches.label: Claymorphic
patches.blurb: Soft extruded plane — directional light top-left, shadow bottom-right, generous radius. Content sits in it; it is never a button.

patches.label: Cyber
patches.blurb: Cyan neon — a glow bloom, a top wash, a bright thin edge. Rides on top of a base.

patches.label: Retro
patches.blurb: CRT amber — sharp corners, a chunky amber edge, a scanline wash. Rides on top of a base.
